title: How War, Crisis and External Pressure Become Reconfiguration Forces
summary: War, crisis and external pressure can all force systems to reallocate resources, but they enter through different channels. War concentrates mobilization, crisis exposes internal vulnerabilities, and external pressure changes the set of available choices.

blocks.text: War, crisis and external pressure can all force systems to reallocate resources, but they enter through different channels. War concentrates mobilization, crisis exposes internal vulnerabilities, and external pressure changes the set of available choices.

Read together, the sections show how pressure can move from event to structure. Some systems restore prior arrangements, some create temporary exceptions, and some turn emergency arrangements into durable institutions or capabilities.

This article uses only definitions and structural relations in the completed Book VI manuscript. Conceptual boundaries are not presented as additional historical facts, and no new causal claims are added beyond the manuscript.
